findings.title: Pending review chips render bare 'review' — both normative strip scenarios show 'review ⟲'
findings.recommendation: The requirement's canonical strip (spec :73) and both scenarios (:89 staging explore; the mid-apply example) render pending review chips as 'review ⟲' — the loop glyph is part of the chip's identity, with N appended only when iterations exist. renderStrip currently composes ['review', detail, glyph] where detail is absent at 0 iterations, so the live render shows '→ review → archive' (verified on this repo). Fix the text render: review chips always carry ⟲ ('review ⟲' at 0 iterations, 'review ⟲6 ✓' with count+gate); the JSON chip keeps detail absent at 0 (the array is data, the ⟲ identity is the text grammar). Update the CLI test assertions to the scenario literals.

findings.title: WAITING external line inserts the mode word inside the spec's quoted literal
findings.recommendation: The requirement (spec :169) and the concurrent-handoff scenario (:185) render `N external review(s) packaged, M returned` — no mode word inside the phrase. deriveWaiting renders '2 external proposal review(s) packaged, 1 returned', which does not contain the normative literal. Align the render: emit the exact literal, appending the mode OUTSIDE the quoted phrase if desired for per-mode disambiguation (counting stays per change+mode either way), e.g. '<name>: 2 external review(s) packaged, 1 returned (proposal)'. Update the module test assertion to the literal.
